name: triggers
instructions: You can schedule work for later in this session. `trigger_wake` takes exactly one of `after`, `at` or `every`; `every` is a cron expression. `trigger_on_exit` runs a command and wakes you when it ends. Call `trigger_list` to see what is pending — you will not remember what you scheduled once it falls out of context. Triggers fire only while cxagent is running.

tools.name: trigger_wake
tools.description: Schedules a prompt to be sent to you later in this session. Set EXACTLY ONE of after, at or every — the call is refused if you set none or more than one. `every` is a five-field cron expression, not a duration. The prompt arrives as a fresh turn with no conversation around it, so write it for a reader who has forgotten why it was scheduled.

after.description: A delay from now: an integer and one unit suffix, s/m/h/d. "90m", "2h". No compound forms.

at.description: A moment, local time: "2026-09-10 09:00" or "2026-09-10T09:00". An explicit offset wins.

every.description: A five-field cron expression: minute hour day-of-month month day-of-week. "0 9 * * 1-5".

prompt.description: What to send you when it fires. Written for a reader with no context.

tools.name: trigger_list
tools.description: The triggers pending in this session: id, when each next fires, and the first line of its prompt. This is how you find out what you scheduled, since nothing else tells you.

tools.name: trigger_update
tools.description: Replaces a trigger's schedule and prompt, KEEPING its id — which is what makes it different from cancel-and-recreate, since a recreated trigger loses the id a user has already seen. Takes the same arguments as trigger_wake and obeys the same exactly-one-of rule.

after.description: A delay from now: an integer and one unit suffix, s/m/h/d.

prompt.description: What to send you when it fires.

tools.name: trigger_cancel
tools.description: Stops a pending trigger. Takes an id from trigger_list.

tools.name: trigger_on_exit
tools.description: Runs a command UNATTENDED until it exits or times out, then wakes you. Fires on ANY exit, whatever the code — a CI watch that exits non-zero is precisely when waking matters. The exit code and the command's output are APPENDED to your prompt automatically, so say what to DO with them rather than how to format them.

command.description: The command to run and wait on, e.g. gh run watch 12345.

timeout.description: How long to wait before giving up, in the same units after takes: "30m", "2h". Required.

prompt.description: What to send you when it ends. The exit code and output are appended for you.

commands.name: triggers-update
commands.summary: Change a trigger, keeping its id
